design_summary.purpose: Single-clock FPGA-friendly PWM LED demo for board prototyping, producing a visible breathing/fading effect on one LED using a slow counter-derived update tick, an 8-bit PWM counter, an 8-bit duty-cycle register, and a direction bit.
design_summary.operating_model: The design accepts the board clock clk, free-runs an internal 8-bit PWM carrier counter, and compares that counter against an 8-bit duty-cycle register to drive led. A much slower internal counter generates an update enable that steps the duty-cycle register up or down by one on each tick. The direction bit toggles only at the duty-cycle endpoints so the LED brightness repeatedly ramps from dim to bright and back again. The implementation is intended to remain fully synthesizable for Lattice FPGA open-source flows and to avoid ASIC-only, testbench-only, or vendor-specific constructs.

external_interfaces.name: clk
external_interfaces.purpose: Single board clock input for all sequential behavior.

external_interfaces.name: led
external_interfaces.purpose: Single LED output driven by the PWM comparison result to create visible brightness modulation.

module_architecture.name: pwm_fpga_demo
module_architecture.role: Top-level synthesizable FPGA demo module and sole architectural boundary described by the source specification.
responsibilities: Accept the single board clock input clk.
Generate an internal slow timing event from a counter to control the breathing rate.
Maintain an 8-bit PWM counter for brightness modulation.
Maintain an 8-bit duty-cycle register that is slowly incremented and decremented.
Maintain a direction bit that toggles at the duty-cycle endpoints.
Drive led with the PWM comparison result to produce visible brightness modulation.
Remain compatible with Lattice FPGA open-source synthesis and place-and-route flows.
interface_notes: The module exposes only clk as an input and led as an output.
No external reset port is present; startup behavior relies on FPGA-compatible initialization semantics or implicit power-up initialization.
The LED output is assumed active-high unless board-specific starter constraints indicate otherwise.
The slow update mechanism is counter-derived rather than based on clock division primitives.
Board-specific starter pin constraints are not part of the RTL module interface and are generated separately after board selection.
ownership_notes: The PWM carrier, slow update tick, duty-cycle stepping, and direction reversal behavior are internally owned by the top module.
No memories, vendor primitives, delays, real-number types, DPI, or testbench-only code are part of the described implementation.
Starter pin constraints are external integration artifacts and must be reviewed before hardware programming.

data_flow_summary: clk feeds all internal sequential state.
A free-running 8-bit PWM counter increments continuously on clk to form the brightness carrier.
The PWM counter is compared against the 8-bit duty-cycle register to determine led on/off state.
A much slower internal counter derives an update tick that steps the duty-cycle register.
When the direction bit indicates up-counting, the duty-cycle register increments by one on each update tick until the maximum boundary is reached.
When the direction bit indicates down-counting, the duty-cycle register decrements by one on each update tick until the minimum boundary is reached.
The direction bit toggles only when the duty-cycle register reaches its minimum or maximum boundary, creating a repeating fade-in/fade-out pattern.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single-clock design using clk only. All sequential behavior is synchronous to this board clock. The slow breathing update is derived internally from a counter so the brightness envelope changes far more slowly than the PWM carrier.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: No external reset port is used. The design shall rely on FPGA-compatible initialization semantics or synthesizable power-up initialization to place registers into a safe demo state: duty cycle at a defined low value or near minimum brightness, direction set to count upward, PWM counter at zero, and slow counter at zero. If deterministic startup requires explicit initial values in the selected flow, those values must remain static and synthesizable.

integration_notes: The generated RTL is intended for lint, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr place-and-route, timing review, and bitstream handoff.
The breathing rate should be human-visible and is expected to be produced by a counter-derived enable rather than a dedicated clock divider primitive.
Board-specific starter pin constraints must be generated only after the target board is selected.
Use PCF constraints for iCE40 targets and LPF constraints for ECP5 targets.
Starter constraints are for bring-up only and must be reviewed before programming physical hardware.
